query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Active-learning Deep Neural Network Potential for HEAs
generation.material_initial_state: Refractory high-entropy alloy (e.g., TiZrTaHfNb or high-entropy carbonitrides) in a mixed solid and ab initio liquid state near high melting temperatures (~3000–5000 K)
generation.intervention: Implement an active-learning DeepMD potential that is iteratively trained on ab initio configurations obtained from both the solid and liquid phases
generation.conditions: Simulations conducted under NPT ensemble at temperatures between 3000 K and 5000 K, covering a range of refractory HEA compositions
generation.structural_mediator: Iterative active-learning sampling of local atomic environments that dynamically refines the potential’s representation of disordered liquid configurations
generation.mechanism: Active learning increases the reference–target phase-space overlap by incorporating diverse and underrepresented atomic configurations from ab initio data, thus reducing thermodynamic integration (TI) path mismatch
generation.predicted_outcome: A reduction in the TI path mismatch by an estimated 30–50% relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, leading to more accurate free-energy differences and melting temperature predictions
generation.baseline: TOR-TILD implementation using static EAM potentials
generation.boundary: Applicable for alloys with up to five principal elements and temperatures between ~3000 K and ~5000 K; may not extend to systems with non-metallic bonding or extreme chemical ordering
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of TI path reduction is approximate and depends on the quality and diversity of the active-learning training set

falsification_experiment.design: Perform two-phase simulations on a representative HEA sample using both the active-learning DeepMD potential and the baseline EAM potential in a TOR-TILD framework. Compare the free-energy integration paths and predicted melting temperatures.
measurements: Quantitative TI path mismatch (e.g., integrated free-energy differences)
Melting temperature predictions compared to direct ab initio values
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the active-learning potential does not reduce the TI path mismatch by at least 30% and does not improve melting temperature predictions within defined error margins relative to the EAM baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Training of deep neural network (DNN) potential was performed by using the DP-GEN package, which was previously successfully used for training of DNN potentials and simulations. Here the interactive or active learning process is used. The learning process consists of iterations, each iteration is divided into three stages: training, exploration, and labelling. In the first iteration, small datasets are generated from ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD) calculations (see (1) in the Fig. 1). In this step, we considered HECN structure in the crystalline and liquid states, and for each structure we performed AIMD simulations at a constant temperature of 3500 K during the 200 steps with a timestep of 1.5 fs. AIMD simulations were performed in the VASP code. This training set was used to obtain pre-trained DMD1 potential (see (2) in the Fig. 1). At the next stage (exploration) we used the LAMMPS package to perform classical molecular dynamics simulations with the pre-trained potential and select candidates for further training. We used two MD simulations that have followed in succession one after the other.

The melting temperature together with supercooling and superheating temperatures of a number of high-entropy carbonitrides (TiZrTaHfNb)CxN1−x with different concentrations of carbon substituted by nitrogen are calculated. The deep learning DeepMD potential is trained on the number of DFT calculations in order to accurately describe both the liquid and solid phases of the considered high-entropy carbonitrides. A new computational procedure is developed and applied to determine the melting hysteresis and melting temperature of HECN using active learning techniques. Heating and cooling curves for HECNs are calculated and carefully analyzed in order to determine the main trends in changes of melting temperatures with respect to nitrogen content. Pair correlation analysis is employed to explain the enhancement of the melting temperature of carbonitrides with small amounts of nitrogen. The obtained data indicates the potential of applications of high-entropy carbonitrides as promising hard and refractive materials for protective coatings of various equipment which operates at extreme conditions.

Classical MD simulations are unable to provide quantitatively accurate predictions of mechanical deformation for these multi-element alloys due to the lack of robust intermolecular potentials. Thus, earlier efforts in the literature have primarily resorted to computationally-expensive and system-size-limiting first-principles calculations, which are restricted in scope for understanding the deformation dynamics of very large systems. New potentials would enable a classical treatment of such alloys and allow us to examine much larger material domains consisting of several thousands of atoms. Here, we derive relevant force-field parameters for a model quinary Al0.1CrCoFeNi HEA shown in Fig. 1, using the available ternary Embedded Atom Method (EAM) and Lennard-Jones (LJ) potentials. Structural properties (e.g., lattice constant, ‘a0’, and bulk modulus, ‘B’) are calculated for our model HEA using MD simulations; we then validate our force-field potentials by the comparison with available experiments and new first-principles Korringa-Kohn-Rostoker (KKR) - Coherent Potential Approximation (CPA) electronic-structure predictions. papers.title: Melting simulations of high-entropy carbonitrides by deep learning potentials.
papers.system: High-entropy carbonitrides (TiZrTaHfNbCxN1-x) in both solid and liquid phases
papers.approach: Development and active-learning training of deep neural network (DeepMD) interatomic potentials based on ab initio molecular dynamics data at high temperatures (~3500 K) to simulate melting processes
papers.findings: The deep-learning potential, trained with an active-learning scheme, accurately reproduced melting, superheating, and supercooling phenomena. It demonstrated that MLIPs can capture the wide variety of atomic configurations present at high temperatures and different compositions.
papers.mechanism: The active-learning procedure iteratively refines the potential to sample configuration space in both the solid and liquid phases, thereby improving reference–target phase-space overlap relative to more rigid EAM references; it does so by dynamically incorporating new configurations from ab initio calculations.

papers.title: Atomistic clustering-ordering and high-strain deformation of an Al0.1CrCoFeNi high-entropy alloy.
papers.approach: Use of classical molecular dynamics with potentials derived from existing ternary Embedded Atom Method (EAM) and Lennard-Jones models, benchmarked against first-principles KKR-CPA results
papers.findings: While EAM and related empirical potentials reproduced some structural properties and deformation behaviors, they demonstrated limitations in representing the full configurational complexity inherent in multicomponent HEAs, especially under extreme conditions and for transitions between liquid and solid states.
papers.mechanism: EAM potentials employ fixed functional forms that are less adaptable to the vast configurational variety found in liquid phases; the work contrasts with MLIP approaches that allow active sampling and active updating to capture atomic diversity.

papers.title: Ab initio framework for deciphering trade-off relationships in multi-component alloys.
papers.approach: Integration of CPA with actively learned Moment Tensor Potentials (MTPs) to compute elastic constants, misfit volumes, and defect properties over the entire composition space
papers.findings: This combined ab initio and machine learning framework accurately captured configurational effects and trends across composition ranges, especially for properties that are sensitive to local relaxations in both the solid state and, by implication, the liquid state near melting.
papers.mechanism: The active learning routine tailors the ML potentials to cover under-represented regions of phase space, which is crucial for improving phase-space overlap, although the focus was on solid properties, it supports the concept that adaptive potentials can overcome limitations of static reference models like EAM.

established: Machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) can be trained actively to capture a wide variety of atomic configurations in complex alloys, including both solid and liquid states near high melting temperatures.
Traditional EAM references lack the flexibility to represent the many atomic configurations in ab initio liquids, especially in multicomponent high-entropy alloys.

approaches_tried.approach: Use of empirical embedded-atom method (EAM) potentials (and associated force fields including Lennard-Jones)
approaches_tried.outcome: Successful reproduction of certain structural properties and deformation behavior in HEAs, but with limitations in configurational sampling and phase-space overlap, particularly in the liquid state.

approaches_tried.approach: Active-learning-based deep neural network potentials (e.g., DeepMD)
approaches_tried.outcome: Demonstrated high accuracy in melting simulations, with improved ability to capture diverse atomic configurations in both solid and liquid states.

mechanisms: Active learning and iterative training enable MLIPs to include new configurations from ab initio data, thereby dynamically expanding the configuration space coverage.

Machine learning potentials approach the free-energy landscape more accurately by closely matching the ab initio representations of both solid and liquid phases, reducing thermodynamic integration path mismatches.
disagreements: There is debate over whether fixed-form potentials like EAM can ever be adequately corrected to capture the configurational complexity of ab initio liquids, versus the need for fully adaptive ML-based approaches.
Some works emphasize using larger supercells and averaging techniques with EAM, while others show that active learning MLIPs provide a more scalable and accurate solution.
open_questions: Can a single methodological intervention—namely, an active-learning-based MLIP—systematically bridge the configurational gap between the ab initio liquid and the reference potential, especially for high-melting multicomponent alloys?
What is the quantitative reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch, relative to TOR-TILD’s use of EAM references, when using MLIPs?
How broadly applicable is the intervention across different composition ranges and temperature regimes (e.g., refractory HEAs and high-entropy carbonitrides)?
What decisive free-energy benchmarks can be established to falsify the hypothesis that the new MLIP leads to superior phase-space overlap?
opportunities: Apply an active-learning scheme to develop deep neural network potentials that are trained explicitly on both solid and liquid phase configurations, particularly at temperatures close to and above melting.
Quantify the improvement in reference–target phase-space overlap by comparing thermodynamic integration paths (e.g., using TOR-TILD) between standard EAM references and the new MLIP reference.
Extend the methodology to a range of refractory HEAs (e.g., TiZrTaHfNb-based alloys) and high-entropy carbonitrides, explicitly mapping composition and temperature ranges from ~3000 K to ~5000 K.
Leverage supporting evidence from elemental and binary systems (e.g., Ta-Cr, Ta-V binaries) where rigorous thermodynamic models have been benchmarked, to validate the MLIP performance.

Design a decisive free-energy benchmark test, such as a direct comparison of predicted melting temperatures or phase transition free energies obtained with the new MLIP versus ab initio results, to falsify the hypothesis if discrepancies exceed a defined threshold.

directions.direction: Active-learning-based deep neural network potentials (e.g., DeepMD) to capture the diverse ab initio configurations in both the solid and liquid states.
directions.type: Machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) development via active learning
directions.assessment: This approach directly addresses the limitation of EAM’s fixed functional form by iteratively incorporating new configurations from ab initio simulations. Evidence shows that active-learning methods improve phase-space overlap (see PMC11576752::web::007::training_of_machine_learning_potential, PMC11576752::web::023::conclusions). It is well supported by known physics and is feasible for HEAs near high melting temperatures.

directions.direction: Hybrid delta-learning combining EAM with a machine-learning correction term that adjusts for liquid-state configurational diversity.
directions.assessment: This method builds on the established EAM framework by adding a corrective ML component, potentially offering improved configurational representation. Evidence from MLIP and clustering studies (e.g., PMC4976365::web::000::abstract) supports its likelihood to enhance phase-space overlap, though it is more complex to calibrate.

directions.direction: On-the-fly adaptive reweighting of interatomic potentials during MD simulations to update potential parameters when encountering high-uncertainty configurations.
directions.type: Adaptive simulation protocol with real-time potential updating
directions.assessment: By actively monitoring the configuration space, this method could continuously improve phase-space overlap. It leverages uncertainty quantification from active learning (PMC11275555::web::035::discussion) but requires robust real-time assessments. Its feasibility depends on the efficiency of triggering updates.

directions.direction: Extension of actively learned Moment Tensor Potentials (MTPs) specifically tailored and trained on both solid and liquid ab initio data for HEAs.
directions.type: Machine learning interatomic potential (MLIP) with alternative descriptor (MTP)
directions.assessment: MTPs have already shown promise in capturing complex configurational effects in multicomponent alloys (PMC11275555::web::005::introduction). Actively learning them for the liquid state can improve phase-space overlap relative to static EAM potentials. This approach is feasible and well supported but would need careful training set design.
